clue.text: Get by policeman close to turnstile

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is wanted

blocks.note: cop is slang for a police officer
the last letter of turnstile

explanation.surface: A constable sidles up to a turnstile, perhaps to slip through without paying.
explanation.definitionFit: To get by is to manage or survive on limited means, which is a synonym of the answer.

clue.text: Film Miguel's mansion on one of the Costas?

blocks.note: casa is Spanish for house; Miguel is a Spanish name
the Costa Blanca is a Spanish coastline

explanation.surface: A Spaniard's villa on one of Spain's holiday coasts.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spanish name tells the solver to give the Spanish word for house.
explanation.definitionFit: Casablanca is the 1942 Hollywood classic starring Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman, an example of a movie.

clue.text: Choose to get rid of a mattock

blocks.note: to pick is to choose
to axe is to cut or dismiss

explanation.surface: Someone decides to throw out an old digging tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattock is a heavy digging tool with a blade like a pick, closely matching this tool.

clue.text: Family shield chosen — cute, redesigned

indicators.note: something redesigned has had its parts laid out afresh, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone picks a family crest and then gives it a cuter makeover.
explanation.definitionFit: An escutcheon is the shield in heraldry on which a family's coat of arms is displayed.

clue.text: Singer, rare, needs to be trained

indicators.note: training reshapes something into a new form, so these letters must be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An unusual vocalist requires voice coaching.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenader sings to a loved one, usually beneath a window, so is a kind of vocalist.

clue.text: Speak in golf club with no hint of pretentiousness

indicators.note: a hint is only a trace, so just the opening letter of the next word is meant
with no says something is taken away and missing

blocks.note: the club used on the green
the first letter of pretentiousness

explanation.surface: Instruction to talk in the golf clubhouse without showing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Golf club' looks like the venue; it is the club in the bag.
explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to say something aloud, a synonym of speak.

clue.text: Express a very different opinion on huge canteens, possibly

indicators.note: possibly suggests one of several arrangements, so these letters can be reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone completely revises their view about vast staff dining halls.
explanation.definitionFit: To change one's tune is the idiom for switching one's stated attitude or position.

clue.text: Choose artist to portray mythical being

blocks.note: to elect is to choose by vote
RA is a Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A casting call: pick a painter to depict a creature of legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is a figure of Greek legend, daughter of Agamemnon, who sought revenge for his murder.

clue.text: Want work, by the sound of it

indicators.note: judging by sound means the word is taken as heard, not as written

blocks.note: to knead is to work dough or clay with the hands

explanation.surface: Someone apparently looking for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Want work' reads as being after a job; work is the verb for handling dough.
explanation.definitionFit: To want something can mean to lack or require it, which is a synonym for need.

clue.text: Number involved with tough lad in scuffle

indicators.note: involved means tangled up, so these letters are entangled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Several people mix it with a hard boy in a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: Rough-and-tumble as a noun is disorderly fighting or play, much like a scuffle.

clue.text: Gullible person reportedly gets help

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the word is judged on its sound

blocks.note: a sucker is someone easily fooled

explanation.surface: A naive person is said to be receiving assistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Succour is assistance given in time of hardship, so it is a synonym of help as a noun.

clue.text: Swing-like apparatus with net added to help, we hear

indicators.note: what we hear is a spoken sound, so the last word counts by how it is pronounced

blocks.note: a net is a device for catching, a trap
to ease is to help or relieve

explanation.surface: Circus talk: a trapeze, with a safety net added to help the performer.
explanation.walkthrough: The net looks part of the circus picture, but it is just the first chunk; the safety net under a trapeze makes the surface neat.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a bar hung from two ropes that acrobats swing on, so it is an apparatus resembling a swing.

clue.text: Victor has them dressing down clever son outside

indicators.note: outside says the clever-son pair sits around the other piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: bright means intelligent
S is the standard abbreviation for son
ragging is teasing or scolding someone

explanation.surface: A clever son is given a telling-off out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victor' looks like a man's name, but here it is simply a winner. The clever son splits as B...RIGHTS around the scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: The winner of a contest earns the entitlement to boast, which is the idiom for what a victor possesses.

clue.text: Terms used by cryptic setters shown round margin

indicators.note: cryptic means puzzling and disguised, so these letters are scrambled
shown round means wrapped around another piece, holding it inside

blocks.note: taken as written
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: A note on the jargon crossword compilers use around the edges of a puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terms' suggests words used by setters, but it means academic periods; 'cryptic setters' is self-referential misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A trimester is one of three divisions of the school or university year, so a term.

clue.text: A queen consort, one leaving Egyptian port

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so that letter departs from the longer word

blocks.note: I is the Roman numeral one
the great port city on Egypt's Mediterranean coast

explanation.surface: A royal wife departs from a harbour in Egypt.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexandra of Denmark was the wife of King Edward VII, and so a British queen consort.

clue.text: Extremely clever Italian in truck, sort of appraiser

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters count
in says the first pieces sit inside the vehicle word

blocks.note: the first and last letters of clever
IT is a standard abbreviation for Italian
artic is British slang for an articulated lorry, a large truck

explanation.surface: A sharp Italian riding in a lorry is some kind of valuer.
explanation.definitionFit: An art critic judges the merits of paintings and exhibitions, which is one particular kind of appraiser.

clue.text: One short tune being broadcast

indicators.note: a short word has been cut down, losing its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
an air is a melody

explanation.surface: A single brief melody is going out on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that is on air is being transmitted live, the idiom for being broadcast.

clue.text: Daily delivery, primarily of beet

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: a daily or char is a British cleaning lady who comes in each day
the first letter of delivery

explanation.surface: A daily delivery made up mainly of beetroot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' reads as an adjective for the delivery, but it is a noun: a daily is a cleaner, also called a charwoman or char.
explanation.definitionFit: Chard, or Swiss chard, is a leafy variety of the beet plant grown for its leaves and stalks.

clue.text: A nasty threat, in reality

indicators.note: nasty suggests something turned bad, so these letters are twisted out of shape

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone muses that an ugly menace is, really, genuine.
explanation.definitionFit: At heart is the idiom for fundamentally, in one's true nature, so it means essentially or really.

clue.text: Swine by embankment in very large port

blocks.note: a swine is a contemptible person, a rotter
a dam is a barrier bank holding back water

explanation.surface: A pig is standing by the sea wall in a big harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swine' looks like a farm animal; it is the insult, a nasty man.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotterdam in the Netherlands is one of the largest seaports in the world.

clue.text: Writer said it stupidly about Rangers

indicators.note: done stupidly means done in a muddled way, so these letters are jumbled
about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go around the other piece

blocks.note: taken as written
R is an abbreviation for Rangers, as in football club results

explanation.surface: A journalist made a foolish remark about Rangers football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A diarist keeps a daily journal, so is a particular kind of writer.

clue.text: Supports arrests — hold-ups cracked?

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so these letters are broken and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A police report: arrests made, and the robberies solved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracked' sounds like detectives solving the hold-ups; it asks for the letters to be broken up.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoulder straps hold up garments or bags, so they are things that support.

clue.text: Large pot used by soldiers in the southern states of the USA

definitions.text: the southern states of the USA

blocks.note: first meaning: a big iron cooking pot used in army camps

blocks.clueFragment: the southern states of the USA
blocks.note: second meaning: the nickname for the old Confederate South

explanation.surface: Army cooking gear spotted in the American South.
explanation.walkthrough: The army pot comes from Hindi degchi, a cooking vessel; the region's nickname is unrelated.
explanation.definitionFit: A dixie is a military cooking pot, and Dixie is also the familiar name for the Southern United States.

clue.text: Czechoslovakia's capital

indicators.note: the possessive says the capital belongs to the country's name, lying within it

blocks.note: found in the middle of the country's name

explanation.surface: A question about the seat of government of the former Czechoslovakia.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface asks for Prague, but the capital sits within the name itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the seat of government of Norway, so it is a national capital city.

clue.text: Makeshift stand in cleaner cubicle?

blocks.note: soap is a cleaning agent
a box is a small enclosed compartment

explanation.surface: Someone asks if a temporary stand is sitting in a cleaning cupboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' suggests a person who cleans, but it is the substance used for cleaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Street orators once stood on an upturned crate for soap, so the word means an improvised platform.

clue.text: One hundred and ten I fiddled in annuity scheme

indicators.note: fiddled means tampered with, so those letters are interfered with and rearranged

blocks.note: a ton is slang for a hundred
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone cooked the books on an annuity, fiddling a hundred and ten.
explanation.definitionFit: A tontine is a pooled investment in which members draw an annuity and the last survivor takes everything.

clue.text: Faltering, hence often unwilling to commit oneself

indicators.note: faltering means stumbling and unsteady, so the following letters wobble into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A wavering person, who therefore often avoids making up their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faltering' reads as part of the definition, since it means much the same thing, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting on the fence is the idiom for staying neutral and refusing to take a side.

clue.text: Regretful miss is in Camelot I see

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: found across the junction of the words

explanation.surface: A sad young lady is at King Arthur's court, I notice.
explanation.walkthrough: Cole Porter's song 'Miss Otis Regrets' makes her the regretful miss.
explanation.definitionFit: The title character of the Cole Porter song regrets she cannot lunch, so she is a remorseful unmarried lady.
